_meta.plan_types: Who sets the appeal rules depends on the plan, not just the state. Fully insured job plans and individual/ACA Marketplace plans bought in a state follow that state's rules and its insurance department. Self-funded employer plans (most large employers; check the plan document or SBC for "self-funded"/"ERISA") follow federal rules: internal appeal under DOL/ERISA, then external review through the federal process or the plan's contracted IROs; state insurance departments cannot help, but DOL EBSA (askebsa.dol.gov, 1-866-444-3272) can. Government/church plans may differ. Medicare (Original and Medicare Advantage) uses Medicare's federal appeal levels. Medicaid/CHIP uses the state Medicaid agency's fair hearing system (managed care members must usually appeal to the plan first). Federal employee (FEHB) plans go to OPM.
_meta.federal_defaults: ACA internal appeal: file within 180 days of the denial. External review: generally within 4 months of the final internal denial (federal process and most state processes); urgent cases can be expedited (decision within 72 hours). Medicaid fair hearing: states may allow up to 90 days from the notice mailing date (42 CFR 431.221); Medicaid managed care: appeal to plan within 60 days, then fair hearing within 120 days of the plan decision. Medicare Advantage: request plan reconsideration within 65 days. Original Medicare: redetermination within 120 days.
sources: CMS external review status table (updated July 9, 2024): https://www.cms.gov/cciio/resources/files/external_appeals

State rules/pages checked: AL 560-X-3-.03; AZ R9-34-107; NJ DMAHS 26-06; RI staycovered.ri.gov; SD ARSD 67:17:02:04; OK OAC 317:2-1-2; WI DHA handbook; ME 144-101-I-1.24; NE 464-1-018; VT Health Connect; DE DMMA notice; UT DHHS manual 125-1; MI MOAHR brochure; MO FSD IM-4; WY Medicaid Ch. 4

_meta.caveats: Not legal advice. The deadline printed on the person's own denial notice controls; when in doubt, file sooner. medicaid_days is the standard window for state-agency (eligibility/fee-for-service) notices; managed care members typically get 120 days after the plan's own appeal decision. Some states count from the notice date, others from receipt or mailing (a few add ~3-5 mailing days). The federal HHS external review process was temporarily unavailable in July 2026 (reopened July 31, 2026; affected deadlines extended to Oct 2, 2026). Complaint and Medicaid URLs were compiled Oct 2026 and some are top-level agency pages; agencies reorganize sites often, so re-check links periodically. Entries marked UNVERIFIED or "believed" in note need confirmation before launch.
